thread:
Anna: heads up — seeing a correlated spike of failed GPU node decrypts in eu-west-1 and a bunch of provisioned nodes stuck in Pending. Started ~10m ago. errors show KMS decryption denied and TCP resets to privatelink endpoint.
Mike: ugh, did anyone touch the vpc firewall or nat rules?
Sasha: I pushed the firewall tightening PR an hour ago — it added a default-deny egress + explicit allow to our audit shipper. I did a quick verification in staging but not full region sweep.
Anna: logs show packets dropped to 10.2.89.34:443 (keystore-proxy) and KMS endpoint 10.2.12.9. stack traces: `keystore: decrypt denied: AccessDenied` then `node-agent: failed to finish bootstrap, gpu-pool evicting`.
Maya: infra-bot shows a canary deploy of fw-policy-2026-03-01 at 1738884000, rollout to eu-west marked complete by `deploy-bot` 9m ago.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: fw-policy-2026-03-01 rolled to eu-west-1 (canary -> 100%). No automatic rollback.
Ryan: if egress to privatelink was restricted we probably cut off the keystore tunnel. Keystore is a privnet service on the same VPC that talks over NACL/SGs. The KMS grant should have fallen back to regional endpoint but that path is NATGW-bound — which we also tightened.
Mike: timeline suggests firewall change -> NATGW deny -> nodes can't reach keystore -> KMS decrypt calls fail -> nodes can't mount disk keys -> GPU nodes stuck.
Sasha: my intent was to prevent noisy audit egress; I scoped allow to `audit-shipper.internal:443` only. I missed the keystore CIDR in policy. I'm owning the rollback if that's OK.
Anna: rollback yes, but we need a faster mitigation: add a short-lived exception for `keystore-proxy` + `kms-regional` CIDRs in the egress policy, and allow NATGW outbound for KMS.
Maya: agree. Also security asked to keep audit logs flowing — we can't just turn off audit egress.
Ryan: can we instead sample audit logs (30%) during recovery to reduce NATGW bandwidth and cost? That reduces immediate egress but keeps security coverage.
Mike: sampling is fine as a stopgap. But note: audit sampling config is in `audit-sampler` service and requires a quick config bump + restart — low risk.
Sasha: I'll patch the fw-rule now: add SG allow for keystore-proxy (10.2.89.0/24) and KMS (10.2.12.0/24), and a natgw exception for `kms.amazonaws.com` out to 443. Pushing in 2m.
Anna: do it in a canary AZ first and monitor `gpu-pool` join rate. Use `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu -w` and `curl` keystore healthcheck.
Maya: putting a quick incident tag in the tracker: INF-3202 (eu-west keystore egress break). I'll notify security and mention cost tradeoff for sampling.
InfraBot: runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/keystore-egress-recovery — step 2 has `iptables` snippets and sample `aws cli` commands.
Mike: for cost, if we open audit egress fully we might incur NATGW data transfer costs; estimate: 1TB/day = ~$80/day across eu-west NATGWs. Suggest sampling + targeted allowlist to minimize.
Sasha: patched and staged to eu-west-a, canary logs show `keystore: handshake success` and one node finished bootstrap.
Anna: good — watching GPU join metric — two nodes joined in the last 60s.
Ryan: security question: long-term we should avoid keeping critical keystore behind private-only CIDRs that require NAT for fallback. Either expose a controlled privatelink endpoint or ensure keystore has direct cross-subnet routing.
Maya: agreed, add architecture ticket to make keystore reachable via privatelink with multi-AZ replicas and documented allowlists. I'll create ARCH-1192.
Mike: postmortem action items: 1) revert overly broad default-deny until exceptions are validated, 2) add automated smoke tests for keystore+KMS during fw rollouts, 3) cost analysis for audit sampling vs full retention, 4) follow up on NATGW egress quotas.
Sasha: noted. I'll open the rollback PR and also add automated smoke to the rollout pipeline.
Anna: thanks everyone. After we stabilize, let's run a quick billing delta for last 24h to see NATGW spikes. Ryan/Mike, can you pair on that?
Mike: can do.
Ryan: yep.
Maya: I'll keep security updated and close INF-3202 when nodes are stable & logs streaming (even if sampled).
Anna: last check: nodes in Ready state now 8 -> 12 in 10m, bootstrap errors trended to zero. Closing thread once we have final billing numbers. :thumbsup:
